picks.rationale: Autodesk Flow Studio's 3D Editor + Canvas turns generative video into a blockable, directable shot pipeline — the most directly workflow-changing release in the pool.
picks.excerpt: Wonder Dynamics co-founder Nikola Todorovic breaks down Autodesk Flow Studio's new 3D Editor + Canvas, which pairs interactive 3D scene construction — characters, mocap, camera tracks, Gaussian-splat environments from World Labs' Marble — with generative 2D video models. The pitch is directable AI filmmaking: block and light the shot in 3D, then finish it in a node-based 2D canvas rather than prompting a whole movie.

picks.rationale: A Kennedy/AFI-convened coalition finally puts a shared vocabulary on where craft-level AI assists end and synthetic performance begins — the line every production will now be judged against.
picks.excerpt: A coalition convened by Kathleen Kennedy and AFI dean Susan Ruskin went public with "Human Generative Workflows," a framework that gives the industry a shared vocabulary for authorship under generative AI. It explicitly separates craft-level AI assists — upscaling, sharpening, markerless mocap, a Resolve color assist — from prompted synthetic performances that substitute for human creative work.

picks.rationale: Freshest item in the pool and the rare AI release aimed at the production office rather than the shot: bid-to-wrap budgets, POs and payroll with an assistant that reads the job's own data.
picks.excerpt: Lineo, built by working commercial producers, launches a single production-management platform covering bid-to-wrap: AICP/APA budgets, calendars, bid packages, POs, payroll and petty cash with live actuals. AI drafts bid letters, parses and logs receipts and POs, and a built-in Production Assistant answers plain-language questions about the job's own data.

picks.rationale: Shot-by-shot filmmaker tests of two unreleased text-to-video models give an early read on what the next generation actually handles, plus a free cinematic reference library to prompt against.
picks.excerpt: Theoretically Media puts two unreleased, codenamed AI video models through filmmaker-style tests and pairs the results with a free cinematic reference library. A useful read on what the next generation of text-to-video is actually good at shot-by-shot.

picks.rationale: DeepMind, AWS and Kling AI moving into Busan's film market alongside seven Korean startups is the clearest sign yet that generative video vendors are becoming Asian film-market infrastructure.
picks.excerpt: Busan's Asian Contents & Film Market unveiled its InnoAsia lineup, pairing Google DeepMind, Amazon Web Services and Kling AI with seven Korean startups, plus a branded-film contest with Hanwha and Innocean. It is one of the clearest signals yet of generative video vendors embedding themselves in Asian film-market infrastructure.
